items.title: Stacking contexts
items.body: z-index only competes within the same stacking context. Positioned elements with a z-index, opacity below 1, transform, filter, and isolation: isolate all create new contexts, and everything inside is layered as one unit relative to its siblings.
items.question: A modal with z-index: 9999 still renders under a header with z-index: 10. Why?
items.answer: The modal sits inside an ancestor that forms its own stacking context at a lower level than the header, so 9999 only applies inside that ancestor. Render the modal near the document root, for example via a portal, or fix the ancestor's stacking.

items.title: Specificity columns
items.body: Specificity compares (ids, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements/pseudo-elements) column by column, so no number of classes beats a single id. Inline styles beat stylesheet selectors, and !important declarations beat normal ones.

items.title: Flex items that will not shrink
items.question: Why does a flex child containing long text or a wide table overflow its container instead of shrinking?
items.answer: Flex items default to min-width: auto, which resolves to their min-content size, so they refuse to shrink below their longest word or widest child. Set min-width: 0 (or overflow: hidden) on the flex item so it can shrink and its content can wrap or truncate.

items.title: Margin pushing the parent
items.question: A child's margin-top: 20px moves its parent down instead of creating space inside the parent. What is going on?
items.answer: The vertical margins of a block parent and its first child collapse when nothing separates them (no border, padding, or new block formatting context). Add padding or a border to the parent, or give it display: flow-root, flex, or grid, which stops the collapse.

items.title: Taming third-party CSS
items.question: Your utility classes keep losing to a third-party stylesheet with more specific selectors. How can cascade layers fix this without !important?
items.answer: Declare layer order, e.g. @layer vendor, base, utilities, and import the vendor CSS into the vendor layer. For normal declarations, layer order beats specificity, so any rule in a later layer wins over earlier layers regardless of selector weight. Unlayered styles beat all layered ones.

items.title: Container queries
items.body: Container queries (@container) style an element based on the size of its container rather than the viewport, so a card can adapt when it sits in a narrow sidebar or a wide column. The ancestor must declare container-type, for example inline-size.
